title: Best countries to work remotely from: 8 picks ranked by visa
summary: Eight countries with real remote-work visas, ranked on income bar, living costs, internet speed and time zone, all checked on official pages. Compare them.
body_markdown:
The best countries to work remotely from right now are Portugal, Malaysia, Thailand, Spain, Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia and the United Arab Emirates. Each one has a visa built for people who earn from abroad, broadband that handles video calls, and a clear income bar you can plan around.


That last point is why this list looks different from the famous rankings. The best-known remote-work index put Germany, Denmark and the US at the top in 2022, yet Germany, the leader, has no visa made for someone paid by a foreign employer. We checked every visa rule, cost figure and internet speed below against government pages and named data sources on 25 November 2026.


## The 8 best countries to work remotely from, at a glance


The order weighs four things: how clear the legal route is, how much you must earn, what daily life costs and how fast the internet is. Use the first table to see whether you qualify and the second to compare daily life.

## Why the famous remote-work rankings send you to the wrong countries


The big indices score how pleasant a country is for remote work, not whether a foreigner can legally do it there. NordLayer's Global Remote Work Index ranked[Germany, Denmark and the US](https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/research-germany-denmark-us-top-123700674.html) as its top three in 2022, judging 66 countries on cybersecurity, economic and social conditions, infrastructure and COVID-19 response.


Germany shows the problem. It has no dedicated digital nomad visa, and its freelance visa usually needs letters of intent from potential German clients,[according to The Local Germany](https://www.thelocal.de/20241108/everything-you-need-to-know-about-working-remotely-in-germany) (November 2024). If your salary comes from London or Lagos, a great score for e-government does not help you get in.


So this list starts with the question the indices skip: is there a visa for you? Only then does it compare rent, broadband and time zones.


## The best countries to work remotely from, ranked


### 1. Portugal: the best all-rounder


Portugal gives you a residence route, not just a long holiday. Its D8 visa for remote work asks for an average monthly income over the last three months of at least four times the Portuguese minimum wage,[per Portugal's visa application centre](https://visa.vfsglobal.com/one-pager/portugal/southafrica/english/pdf/D9-RESIDENCY-VISA-FOR-REMOTE-WORK-DIGITAL-NOMAD-2025.pdf) . With the minimum wage at[€920 in 2026](https://portugal.gov.pt/en/gc25/communication/news/government-increases-minimum-wage-to-920-euros-in-2026) , that is €3,680 a month.


- **Why it ranks first:** a clear legal route, broadband of 243.84 Mbps and London's clock, which also gives you a five-hour head start on New York.
- **Watch out for:** the highest monthly income bar on this list.
- **Best cities:** Lisbon, Porto, Funchal (Madeira).


Before you apply, read our[D8 application guide](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-apply-for-a-digital-nomad-visa-in-portugal) .


### 2. Malaysia: the cheapest place to live


Malaysia has the lowest living costs and rent on this list, and a modest income bar if your job qualifies. The DE Rantau Nomad Pass needs US$24,000 a year (about US$2,000 a month) for tech and digital roles, or US$60,000 for senior non-tech roles such as CEO or legal counsel, according to the[official DE Rantau FAQ](https://www.mdec.my/api/media/file/DE-Rantau_Pass_FAQ_v10.pdf) (version 10, August 2026).


- **Why it ranks high:** a cost of living index of 34.0, rent at 8.5 and a pass of 3 to 12 months, renewable to 24 months in total.
- **Watch out for:** a RM1,080 processing fee, and the FAQ says tax can apply once a remote worker stays 61 days or more.
- **Best cities:** Kuala Lumpur, Penang (George Town), Johor Bahru.


Our[DE Rantau guide](https://grey.co/blog/malaysia-digital-nomad-visa) covers the documents.


### 3. Thailand: the longest visa


Thailand's Destination Thailand Visa lasts five years, the longest on this list. It allows 180 days per entry, extendable once by another 180 days, and asks for at least 500,000 baht in funds and a 10,000 baht fee, per the[Thai foreign ministry](https://image.mfa.go.th/mfa/0/xJ3BrCz2xe/DTV_Infographic.pdf) .


- **Why it ranks high:** low living costs (index 36.8) with broadband faster than the UK's (279.65 Mbps).
- **Watch out for:** you must leave and re-enter after each stay, and UTC+7 means late calls with American teams.
- **Best cities:** Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket.


See our[DTV walkthrough](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-apply-for-the-destination-thailand-visa-thai-digital-nomad-visa) for the application steps.


### 4. Spain: the easiest European income bar


Spain asks for less income than Portugal or Croatia. The bar is 200% of the minimum wage each month, per the[Spanish consulate in New York](https://exteriores.gob.es/Consulados/nuevayork/en/ServiciosConsulares/Paginas/Consular/Visado-de-teletrabajo.aspx) , and with the 2026 minimum wage at[€1,221 over 14 payments](https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/lang/en/presidente/news/Paginas/2026/20260216-minimum-wage-increase.aspx) ,[The Local Spain](https://www.thelocal.es/20260216/confirmed-the-financial-requirements-for-spains-digital-nomad-visa-in-2026) puts the bar at about €2,849 a month.


- **Why it ranks high:** a residence permit of up to three years and 277.98 Mbps broadband.
- **Watch out for:** you need at least three months with your employer or client, the company must be at least a year old, and freelancers can earn no more than 20% from Spanish clients.
- **Best cities:** Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia.


Here is[Spain's application process](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-apply-for-a-digital-nomad-visa-in-spain) , step by step.


### 5. Colombia: the best fit for US clients on a budget


Colombia pairs New York's winter clock with some of the lowest costs here (index 35.6). Its digital nomad visa needs income of at least three times the monthly minimum wage and lasts up to two years, per[Colombia's Ministry of Justice](https://www.minjusticia.gov.co/programas-co/LegalApp/Paginas/Visa-n%C3%B3mada-digital.aspx) .


- **Why it ranks here:** UTC-5 all year, 214.30 Mbps broadband and a two-year stay.
- **Watch out for:** you need a passport from a country that does not need a short-stay visa for Colombia, and the fee is US$177 for Europeans or US$230 for everyone else.
- **Best cities:** Medellín, Bogotá.


### 6. Costa Rica: tax-free remote income


Costa Rica's official tourism board says digital nomads are exempt from income tax. The stay needs US$3,000 a month earned outside Costa Rica (US$4,000 with dependants) and a US$100 fee, per the[official requirements](https://visitcostarica.com/digital-nomads/requirements) .


- **Why it ranks here:** one year, with the option to renew for another, and a time zone one hour behind New York in winter.
- **Watch out for:** the highest cost of living on this list (index 56.8), and you must show a year of bank statements.
- **Best cities:** San José, Santa Teresa, Tamarindo.


Our[Costa Rica guide](https://grey.co/blog/costa-rica-digital-nomad-visa) covers eligibility and costs.


### 7. Croatia: an EU base for non-EU citizens


Croatia offers non-EU citizens up to 18 months in the EU. It asks for at least €3,622.50 a month, or €43,470 in savings for a 12-month stay, per[Croatia's interior ministry](https://mup.gov.hr/aliens-281621/stay-and-work/temporary-stay-of-digital-nomads/286833) , and the accounting firm[Crowe Croatia](https://crowe.com/hr/en-us/blog-page/digitalni-nomadi-u-hrvatskoj) says digital nomads do not pay Croatian income tax.


- **Why it ranks here:** European time, an EU base and a tax break, if you can meet the bar.
- **Watch out for:** the second-highest income bar here, the slowest broadband (136.75 Mbps) and a cap of 18 months.
- **Best cities:** Zagreb, Split.


### 8. United Arab Emirates: no income tax, fastest internet


The UAE has the fastest broadband here (384.51 Mbps) and[no income tax on individuals](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/finance-and-investment/taxation) . Its one-year virtual work residence visa needs proof that you work for an organisation outside the UAE and earn US$3,500 a month, per the[UAE government portal](https://beta.government.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/residence-visas/residence-visa-for-working-outside-the-uae) .


- **Why it ranks here:** UTC+4 sits between Europe and Asia, so you can overlap with both.
- **Watch out for:** the highest rent on this list (index 36.3), close to the US level.
- **Best cities:** Dubai, Abu Dhabi.


## Pick by your clients' time zone


Your clients' clock matters more than the beach, because it sets when you sleep. If a New York client books a 9am call, that is 9am in Bogotá, 2pm in Lisbon and 10pm in Kuala Lumpur during New York's winter.


- **US clients:** Colombia or Costa Rica.
- **UK and European clients:** Portugal, Spain or Croatia.
- **Asian or Australian clients:** Malaysia or Thailand.
- **A mix of Europe and Asia:** the UAE.


Europe moves its clocks forward in summer, while Colombia, Costa Rica, Malaysia, Thailand and the UAE do not. Check the gap in both seasons before you sign a lease.


## How to get paid and prove your income for the visa


Most of these visas ask for bank statements, so the way you get paid shapes your application. Croatia accepts a bank statement showing regular income, Portugal looks at your three-month average, and Costa Rica asks for a year of statements.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best country to work remotely from?


Portugal is the best all-round choice for most remote workers, because its D8 visa is a residence route and its broadband and time zone suit UK and US clients. If your budget is tight and you work in tech, Malaysia is the cheapest place to live on this list and asks for US$24,000 a year.


### Can I work remotely from another country on a tourist visa?


It depends on the country, and many tourist rules say nothing clear about remote work. A visa built for remote workers removes that doubt, which is why every country on this list has one. Our guide to working on a[tourist visa](https://grey.co/blog/can-you-work-remotely-while-travelling-on-a-tourist-visa) explains the risks.


### Can you work remotely from another country permanently?


Not on most remote-work visas alone, because they have end dates: 18 months in Croatia, 24 months in Malaysia and two years in Colombia. Portugal and Spain issue residence permits rather than temporary stays, so they suit people who plan to stay for years.


### What is the cheapest country to work remotely from?


Malaysia is the cheapest country on this list, with a Numbeo cost of living index of 34.0 and a rent index of 8.5 (2026 mid-year). Colombia (35.6) and Thailand (36.8) come next.


## The visa comes first


Portugal, Malaysia and Thailand top this list, but the right pick depends on your income, your passport and your clients' time zone. Start with the table, check the official page for your shortlisted country, and see our[50-plus country list](https://grey.co/blog/a-list-of-50-countries-offering-digital-nomad-visas) if none of these fits, or the[nomad tax guide](https://grey.co/blog/digital-nomad-tax) before you move.


The best country to work remotely from is the one that will let you stay.
